(Le Bénin s’engage pour répondre aux besoins des populations)
Les acteurs du secteur public comme privé en matière de la gestion des ressources en eau se sont réunis, mardi 05 novembre 2024 à l’hôtel Azalaï de Cotonou, dans le cadre de la célébration des journées portes ouvertes sur la Gestion intégrée des ressources en eau. Cette grande assise organisée sous la houlette du ministère de l’énergie, de l’eau et des mines, appuyé par la GIZ, offre un cadre d’échange entre experts dans la perspective d’envisager de solutions satisfaisantes au sujet des besoins en eau qui s’expriment avec acuité dans le rang de la population.
Les Journées Portes Ouvertes sur la Gestion Intégrée des Ressources en Eau (GIRE) s’ouvrent, mardi 05 novembre 2024 à Azalaï hôtel de Cotonou. Organisé par La Direction Générale de l’Eau (DG Eau), cet événement entend donner de la visibilité aux actions entreprises par les acteurs du secteur depuis plus de 20 ans pour une gestion durable des ressources en eau au Bénin. Pour le directeur des eaux, Hounkponou K. Saïd, la GIRE promeut le développement coordonné de l’eau, des terres, et des ressources associées pour un bien-être économique et social équitable, tout en assurant la durabilité des écosystèmes.
Dans ce cadre, l’objectif principal de cette rencontre est de mettre en lumière les progrès de la GIRE et encourager le soutien des partenaires techniques et financiers (PTF). Ensuite, il est aussi question de présenter les initiatives des projets GIRE de la Direction Générale de l’Eau et des partenaires, sensibiliser le public national et international sur le concept de la GIRE, puis souligner l’évolution de la GIRE au Bénin en lien avec les Objectifs de développement Durable (ODD), en particulier l’ODD 6 sur l’eau propre et l’assainissement. Prévu pour durer deux jours, c’est-à-dire les 5 et 6 novembre 2024, cet événement sera axé autour de riches panels thématiques avec à la clé, des stands d’exposition, et des moments de discussion avec les experts du secteur. C’est une manifestation de taille qui a réuni des représentants des ministères de l’énergie de l’eau et des mines, des ONG, des PTF (USAID, Banque Mondiale, etc.), et des institutions académiques, ainsi que des organisations locales et internationales spécialisées en hydrologie et en gestion de l’eau. Ils étaient au total 180 participants, incluant des experts et étudiants ont répondu présents à ce rendez-vous.
Teddy G.
a6.en:
(Benin commits to responding to the needs of the population)
Stakeholders from both the public and private sectors in water resource management met on Tuesday, November 5, 2024, at the Azalaï hotel in Cotonou, as part of the celebration of the open house days on Integrated Water Resources Management. This major gathering, organized under the leadership of the Ministry of Energy, Water and Mines, supported by GIZ, provides a framework for exchange between experts with a view to finding satisfactory solutions to the water needs that are strongly expressed among the population.

The Open House Days on Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) opened on Tuesday, November 5, 2024, at the Azalaï hotel in Cotonou. Organized by the General Directorate of Water (DG Eau), this event aims to give visibility to the actions undertaken by sector stakeholders for more than 20 years for sustainable water resource management in Benin. For the director of water, Hounkponou K. Saïd, IWRM promotes the coordinated development of water, land, and related resources for equitable economic and social well-being, while ensuring the sustainability of ecosystems.

In this context, the main objective of this meeting is to highlight the progress of IWRM and encourage the support of technical and financial partners (TFPs). It also aims to present the IWRM project initiatives of the General Directorate of Water and its partners, raise national and international public awareness of the IWRM concept, and highlight the evolution of IWRM in Benin in connection with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 6 on clean water and sanitation. Scheduled to last two days, namely November 5 and 6, 2024, this event will be built around rich thematic panels, with exhibition booths and discussion sessions with sector experts. It is a major event that brought together representatives from the ministries of energy, water and mines, NGOs, TFPs (USAID, World Bank, etc.), and academic institutions, as well as local and international organizations specializing in hydrology and water management. In total, 180 participants, including experts and students, attended this event.

Teddy G.

MONROVIA, LIBERIA-A congressional advocate for the interests of Africa in the United States is urging the Liberian Government to strengthen its relationships with regional and continental organizations.
According to Mr. Melvin Foote, the current freeze on aid, through USAID, must be seen as a wakeup call for African leaders to work together to reduce the impact such a decision may have on the continent.
In an interview on the “Super Morning Show” on Tuesday, February 4, 2025, the President and Founder of the “Constituency of Africa” based in Washington, D.C. lauded President Joseph Boakai for efforts aimed at improving governance in Liberia.
Mr. Foote said:” The ongoing freeze on aid across the world by the United States government is having an unprecedented humanitarian impact on millions.”
However, Foote stated that country like Liberia stands a chance of weaving out the opportunities for strong partnerships with counterparts on the continent.

Vaccination remains a key tool to prevent severe cases and deaths from COVID-19 infection
Addis Ababa, Ethiopia | Xinhua | The Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) on Friday urged African health authorities to intensify COVID-19 prevention measures amid the emergence of a new variant.
The Africa CDC made the call a day after the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD) in South Africa announced the detection of a new variant, B.1.1.529, of the SARS-COV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19 pandemic. The World Health Organization on Friday classified it as a “Variant of Concern.”
“National health authorities across the continent should reinforce public health and social measures and accelerate immunization of their populations, prioritizing high risk groups, ahead of upcoming new waves of COVID-19 infections,” the agency said in a statement.
It called on African countries to expedite COVID-19 vaccination drive to halt the spread of the virus, saying “vaccines remain a key tool to prevent severe cases and deaths from COVID-19 infection.”
The agency underscored the need to reinforce timely genomic surveillance through coordination with national and regional pathogen genomics laboratories.
As of Saturday, the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases in Africa has reached 8,616,912 with 222,301 deaths and 8,064,499 recoveries, according to the agency.

a198.t:
Communiqué du Conseil des ministres du mercredi 7 mai 2025
A/-Mesures Générales,
- Projets de loi et d’ordonnance
- Projets de décrets
C/-Communications
D/-Divers
A/– MESURES GENERALES
PROJETS DE LOI ET D’ORDONNANCE
- Au titre du Ministère des Affaires Etrangères, de l’Intégration Africaine et des Ivoiriens de l’Extérieur ;
Le Conseil a adopté un projet de loi autorisant le Président de la République à ratifier le Protocole à la Charte Africaine des Droits de l’Homme et des Peuples, relatif aux droits des personnes handicapées en Afrique.
Adopté en janvier 2018 lors de la 30e session ordinaire de la Conférence de l’Union, ce Protocole à la Charte Africaine des Droits de l’Homme et des Peuples, est le premier Traité africain relatif aux droits de l’Homme qui aborde les formes spécifiques de discrimination touchant les personnes handicapées sur le continent, telles que les pratiques, les croyances et les superstitions inappropriées, à l’encontre de ces personnes vulnérables.
La ratification de cette convention permettra de réaffirmer l’engagement de notre pays exprimé dans la Constitution, de promouvoir et de protéger toutes les catégories de Droits de l’Homme, et de consolider spécifiquement les droits des personnes handicapées sur l’ensemble du territoire national.
- Au titre du Ministère de l’Intérieur et de la Sécurité ;
Le Code Electoral, en son article 51, fait obligation à chaque candidat à l’élection du Président de la République de produire une liste d’électeurs consentant à accorder leur parrainage à la candidature, soit un pour cent (01%) de l’électorat local, dans au moins cinquante pour cent (50%) des Districts autonomes et régions.
Sur proposition de la Commission Electorale Indépendante (CEI), cette ordonnance précise que l’électorat local concerné par le parrainage est celui des trente-et-une (31) régions et des deux (02) Districts autonomes d’Abidjan et de Yamoussoukro.
Cette mesure vise à éviter une augmentation du nombre de circonscriptions administratives où les parrainages seraient requis, en raison de l’augmentation du nombre de Districts autonomes de deux (2) à quatorze (14), par l’effet du décret n° 2021-276 du 9 juin 2021 portant création de douze (12) districts autonomes.
PROJETS DE DECRETS
- Au titre du Ministère d’Etat, Ministère de la Fonction Publique et de la Modernisation de l’Administration, en liaison avec le Ministère des Finances et du Budget et le Ministère des Affaires Etrangères, de l’Intégration Africaine et des Ivoiriens de l’Extérieur ;
Le Conseil a adopté un décret portant organisation de la formation continue des fonctionnaires et agents de l’Etat.
En application des dispositions nouvelles du Statut général de la Fonction Publique, qui induisent une mutation importante de l’Administration publique et du Service public, ce décret actualise les modalités d’organisation de la formation continue des fonctionnaires et agents de l’Etat relevant des Institutions, des Ministères, des Etablissements Publics Nationaux et des Collectivités territoriales ou de toute autre structure où des fonctionnaires et agents de l’Etat sont en service.
Plus inclusif que l’ancien dispositif, ce décret introduit diverses innovations, en vue de redynamiser la formation continue et d’offrir à tous les fonctionnaires et agents de l’Etat, sans restriction, des possibilités multiples d’acquérir, de maintenir et d’améliorer leurs compétences pour un service public de qualité.
Il prolonge notamment la durée maximale de la formation continue de longue durée ainsi que celle du congé de formation professionnelle à six (06) ans, sur l’ensemble de la carrière de l’agent, afin de lui permettre de réaliser un projet personnel qui soit en relation avec ses activités professionnelles.
Il institue, en outre, la validation des acquis de l’expérience avec pour objectif de valoriser les compétences-métiers dans l’Administration publique et d’améliorer les performances des services publics.
- Au titre du Ministère des Affaires Etrangères de l’Intégration Africaine et des Ivoiriens de l’Extérieur, en liaison avec le Ministère d’Etat, Ministère de la Défense ;
- Le premier décret porte ratification de l’Accord-Cadre en matière de coopération militaire dans les domaines de la formation, de la technique et de la science entre le Gouvernement de la République de Côte d’Ivoire et le Gouvernement de la République de Türkiye, signé le 26 mars 2015, à Ankara.
Cet accord a été signé à l’occasion de la visite officielle du Président de la République, en Türkiye, en mars 2015.
Cet accord d’intérêt stratégique permettra à nos forces armées de bénéficier de l’expérience de la République de Türkiye en matière d’industrie de la défense, de médecine militaire, de systèmes électroniques de l’information militaire, ainsi qu’en matière d’opérations autres que la guerre, telles que les opérations de maintien de la paix et d’aide humanitaire.
- Le deuxième décret porte ratification de l’Accord de coopération dans le domaine de la formation militaire entre le Gouvernement de la République de Côte d’Ivoire et le Gouvernement de la République de Türkiye, signé le 23 octobre 2024, à Ankara.
Cet accord a été signé en marge du 4e Salon International de la Défense et de l’Aérospatial, tenu en octobre 2024, à Ankara.
Il vise à élever davantage le niveau d’interopérabilité de nos forces armées, notamment dans les domaines d’exercices multinationaux axés sur la lutte contre le terrorisme, la piraterie maritime et les opérations de maintien de paix.
- Au titre du Ministère des Affaires Etrangères, de l’Intégration Africaine et des Ivoiriens de l’Extérieur, en liaison avec le Ministère d’Etat, Ministère de l’Agriculture, du Développement rural et des Productions Vivrières et le Ministère des Finances et du Budget ;
Le Conseil a adopté un décret portant ratification de l’Accord-cadre de vente à tempérament n° CIV-1032, conclu le 26 février 2025, entre la Banque Islamique de Développement (BID) et la République de Côte d’Ivoire, d’un montant total de 65 400 000 Euros, soit quarante-deux milliards huit cent quatre-vingt-dix-neuf millions cinq cent quatre-vingt-sept mille huit cents (42 899 587 800) Francs CFA, pour le financement du projet de développement de la chaîne de valeur du manioc en Côte d’Ivoire.
- Au titre du Ministère des Affaires Etrangères, de l’Intégration Africaine et des Ivoiriens de l’Extérieur, en liaison avec le Ministère d’Etat, Ministère de l’Agriculture, du Développement Rural et des Productions Vivrières, le Ministère de l’Economie, du Plan et du Développement et le Ministère des Finances et du Budget ;
Le Conseil a adopté un décret portant ratification de l’Accord de prêt n° CIV-1032, conclu le 26 février 2025, entre la Banque Islamique de Développement (BID) et la République de Côte d’Ivoire, d’un montant total de trois millions sept cent-soixante-dix mille (3 770 000) Dinars Islamique, soit trois milliards dix-sept millions quatre cent-deux mille deux cents (3 017 402 200) Francs CFA, pour le financement du projet de développement de la chaîne de valeur du manioc en Côte d’Ivoire.
Le projet objet de ces deux (02) accords de prêt a globalement pour objectif d’améliorer la résilience du système de production vivrière et de contribuer au renforcement de la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle.
Plus spécifiquement, le projet vise à rendre plus dynamique la chaîne de valeur du manioc, allant de la production à la transformation et à la commercialisation des produits du manioc, en vue de créer davantage d’opportunités d’emploi, en particulier pour les jeunes et les femmes, et d’accroitre les revenus des ménages œuvrant dans la filière du manioc.
B/– MESURE INDIVIDUELLE
Au titre du Ministère des Affaires Etrangères, de l’Intégration Africaine et des Ivoiriens de l’Extérieur ;
Le Conseil a donné son agrément en vue de la nomination de Monsieur MIRMOHAMMAD MEIGONI Seyed Gholamreza, en qualité d’Ambassadeur Extraordinaire et Plénipotentiaire de la République Islamique d’Iran près la République de Côte d’Ivoire, avec résidence à Abidjan.
C/– COMMUNICATIONS
- Au titre du Ministre de l’Economie, du Plan et du Développement, en liaison avec le Ministère des Finances et du Budget et le Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie ;
Le Conseil a adopté une communication relative à la participation de la Côte d’Ivoire aux Réunions de Printemps du Fonds Monétaire International et du Groupe de la Banque Mondiale, tenues du 21 au 26 avril 2025, à Washington DC, aux Etats-Unis.
Une importante délégation conduite par le Ministre de l’Economie, du Plan et du Développement a pris part à ces assises, qui ont été marquées par les incertitudes de l’économie mondiale, liées au contexte actuel de l’escalade des droits de douane avec une aggravation des tensions commerciales. De sorte que les perspectives de la croissance de l’économie mondiale projetée à 2,8% en 2025 et à 3% en 2026, sont en recul par rapport aux projections antérieures.
En conséquence, les travaux ont recommandé la prudence dans la conduite des politiques économiques et le renforcement de la coopération internationale, en vue de faire baisser les tensions commerciales.
S’agissant de la Côte d’Ivoire, les performances économiques de notre pays ont fait l’objet d’une attention particulière du FMI, du Groupe de la Banque Mondiale et de l’ensemble des acteurs bilatéraux et de ceux du secteur privé. Le FMI, notamment, s’est félicité des performances enregistrées par l’exécution en cours du Programme Economique et Financier signé ensemble, ainsi que du succès de l’émission de l’eurobond en francs CFA.
Les progrès réalisés dans la lutte contre le blanchiment des capitaux et le financement du terrorisme, ainsi que le succès enregistré dans les opérations de gestion de la dette ont été fortement appréciés par tous les partenaires techniques et financiers rencontrés, qui ont réaffirmé leur engagement à poursuivre et à intensifier leur coopération avec notre pays.
- Au titre du Ministère de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme, en liaison avec le Ministère des Finances et du Budget et le Ministère des Affaires Etrangères, de l’Intégration Africaine et des Ivoiriens de l’Extérieur ;
Le Conseil a adopté une communication relative à la candidature d’un Expert ivoirien en Doits de l’Homme aux élections de renouvellement des membres du Comité pour l’élimination de la discrimination raciale des Nations Unies, prévues le 26 juin 2025, à New York, aux Etats-Unis.
Le mandat de notre compatriote Bakary Sidiki DIABY, élu le 24 juin 2021, lors de la 29e session des Etats parties à la Convention internationale sur l’Elimination de toutes les formes de Discrimination raciale des Nations Unies, instituant le Comité d’Experts, expire en juin 2025.
Aussi, le Conseil a instruit le Garde des Sceaux, Ministre de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme et l’ensemble des Ministres concernés, à l’effet de prendre les dispositions idoines pour soutenir la candidature au renouvellement de mandat de notre compatriote, au sein de cet organe international majeur de sauvegarde des Droits de l’Homme.
- Au titre du Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de la Digitalisation, en liaison avec le Ministère de l’Intérieur et de la Sécurité, le Ministère des Finances et du Budget, le Ministère des Affaires Etrangères, de l’Intégration Africaine et des Ivoiriens de l’Extérieur, le Ministère de la Promotion de la Jeunesse, de l’Insertion Professionnelle et du Service Civique et le Ministère de la Culture et de la Francophonie ;
Ivoire Tech Forum est une plateforme à dimension internationale initiée par le Gouvernement, dans le cadre de la Stratégie de la transformation numérique, pour connecter les Startups numériques ivoiriennes et africaines au reste du monde, en mettant en avant les talents, les innovations et les opportunités d’investissement.
Ainsi sont attendus à ce Forum près de cinq cents (500) participants comprenant notamment des startups numériques, des grandes entreprises, des institutions gouvernementales et des investisseurs internationaux.
Ivoire Tech Forum 2025 se déroulera autour du thème « Le numérique au service de tous : comment les nouvelles technologies transforment notre quotidien ».
En outre, afin de répondre au mieux aux enjeux stratégiques actuels du développement numérique, se tiendront des expositions, des panels, des ateliers pratiques, des compétitions de startups et des forums sectoriels, sur la cybersécurité et la protection des données, l’Intelligence Artificielle, l’entrepreneuriat technologique et les Infrastructures technologiques.
- Au titre du Ministère de l’Emploi et de la Protection Sociale
Le Conseil a entendu le compte rendu de la célébration de l’édition 2025 de la Fête du Travail.
A l’occasion de cette célébration, le Premier Ministre a exprimé sa profonde reconnaissance à l’endroit de la vaillante population ivoirienne ainsi qu’à l’ensemble des travailleurs, dont l’abnégation et le labeur portent la croissance et la résilience de l’économie nationale.
Il a tenu à rappeler les importants gains concédés aux travailleurs des secteurs public et privé depuis 2013 et dont les efforts financiers cumulés ressortent à plus de 3.700 milliards de francs CFA.
S'agissant des revendications nouvelles formulées par les Centrales Syndicales, le Premier Ministre a demandé aux syndicalistes de prendre patience et de faire confiance au Gouvernement afin que toutes les revendications soient traitées dans le cadre de procédures centrées sur le dialogue social, de façon à préserver les grands équilibres de l’élan de développement amorcé par notre pays.
Par ailleurs, au cours de la célébration de cette édition de la Fête du Travail, le Premier Ministre a annoncé une mesure dérogatoire exceptionnelle décidée par le Président de la République, permettant l'ouverture des droits d'accès à la CMU au profit des assurés du secteur informel, à compter du 02 mai jusqu'au 31 août 2025, soit pour une durée de quatre (04) mois.
Environ treize (13) millions de primo assurés bénéficieront sans avoir cotisés au préalable des services offerts par la CMU, notamment l’accès aux soins et aux médicaments en payant seulement le ticket modérateur de 30%.
Dans les centres de santé ruraux, la prise en charge dans le cadre de cette mesure est totalement gratuite, les consultations, les actes infirmiers et la dispensation de médicaments à usage ambulatoire sont pris en charge à 100% par l'État.
Le coût de la mise en œuvre de cette décision est évalué à 8,4 milliards de francs CFA.
D- DIVERS
- Le Conseil a entendu le compte rendu du Vice-Président de la République, représentant du Président de la République à la cérémonie d’investiture du Président élu de la République gabonaise, Son Excellence Monsieur Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguéma.
En marge de la cérémonie, le Président de la République gabonaise a accordé une audience au Vice-Président de la République, qui a porté essentiellement sur le renforcement de la coopération entre les deux pays.
- Le prochain Conseil des Ministres se tiendra le 22 mai 2025, à Abidjan.
Fait à Abidjan, le mercredi 07 mai 2025
M. Amadou COULIBALY
Ministre de la Communication, Porte-parole du Gouvernement

Communiqué of the Council of Ministers of Wednesday 7 May 2025

A/- General Measures,
- Draft laws and ordinance
- Draft decrees
C/- Communications
D/- Miscellaneous

A/- GENERAL MEASURES

DRAFT LAWS AND ORDINANCE

- Under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and Ivorians Abroad;

The Council adopted a draft law authorising the President of the Republic to ratify the Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in Africa.

Adopted in January 2018 at the 30th ordinary session of the Assembly of the Union, this Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights is the first African human rights treaty that addresses the specific forms of discrimination affecting persons with disabilities on the continent, such as inappropriate practices, beliefs and superstitions directed against these vulnerable persons.

Ratification of this convention will make it possible to reaffirm our country's commitment, expressed in the Constitution, to promote and protect all categories of human rights, and specifically to consolidate the rights of persons with disabilities throughout the national territory.

- Under the Ministry of the Interior and Security;

The Electoral Code, in its article 51, requires each candidate for the election of the President of the Republic to produce a list of voters consenting to grant their sponsorship to the candidacy, namely one percent (01%) of the local electorate, in at least fifty percent (50%) of the autonomous Districts and regions.

On the proposal of the Independent Electoral Commission (CEI), this ordinance specifies that the local electorate concerned by the sponsorship is that of the thirty-one (31) regions and the two (02) autonomous Districts of Abidjan and Yamoussoukro.

This measure aims to avoid an increase in the number of administrative constituencies where sponsorships would be required, due to the increase in the number of autonomous Districts from two (2) to fourteen (14), by the effect of decree no. 2021-276 of 9 June 2021 creating twelve (12) autonomous districts.

DRAFT DECREES

- Under the Ministry of State, Ministry of the Public Service and Modernisation of the Administration, in conjunction with the Ministry of Finance and Budget and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and Ivorians Abroad;

The Council adopted a decree organising the continuing training of civil servants and State agents.

In application of the new provisions of the General Statute of the Public Service, which bring about a significant transformation of the public Administration and of the public Service, this decree updates the arrangements for organising the continuing training of civil servants and State agents attached to Institutions, Ministries, National Public Establishments and territorial Collectivities or any other structure where civil servants and State agents are in service.

More inclusive than the former system, this decree introduces various innovations, with a view to revitalising continuing training and offering all civil servants and State agents, without restriction, multiple opportunities to acquire, maintain and improve their skills for a quality public service.

In particular, it extends the maximum duration of long-term continuing training as well as that of professional training leave to six (06) years over the whole of the agent's career, in order to allow him or her to carry out a personal project connected with his or her professional activities.

It also institutes the validation of acquired experience, with the objective of valuing job-related skills in the public Administration and improving the performance of public services.

- Under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and Ivorians Abroad, in conjunction with the Ministry of State, Ministry of Defence;

- The first decree concerns the ratification of the Framework Agreement on military cooperation in the fields of training, technology and science between the Government of the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire and the Government of the Republic of Türkiye, signed on 26 March 2015 in Ankara.

This agreement was signed on the occasion of the official visit of the President of the Republic to Türkiye in March 2015.

This agreement of strategic interest will allow our armed forces to benefit from the experience of the Republic of Türkiye in the fields of defence industry, military medicine, military information electronic systems, as well as in operations other than war, such as peacekeeping and humanitarian aid operations.

- The second decree concerns the ratification of the Cooperation Agreement in the field of military training between the Government of the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire and the Government of the Republic of Türkiye, signed on 23 October 2024 in Ankara.

This agreement was signed on the sidelines of the 4th International Defence and Aerospace Exhibition, held in October 2024 in Ankara.

It aims to further raise the level of interoperability of our armed forces, in particular in the areas of multinational exercises focused on the fight against terrorism, maritime piracy and peacekeeping operations.

- Under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and Ivorians Abroad, in conjunction with the Ministry of State, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Food Production and the Ministry of Finance and Budget;

The Council adopted a decree ratifying the Instalment Sale Framework Agreement no. CIV-1032, concluded on 26 February 2025 between the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) and the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire, for a total amount of 65,400,000 Euros, i.e. forty-two billion eight hundred and ninety-nine million five hundred and eighty-seven thousand eight hundred (42,899,587,800) CFA Francs, for the financing of the cassava value chain development project in Côte d'Ivoire.

- Under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and Ivorians Abroad, in conjunction with the Ministry of State, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Food Production, the Ministry of Economy, Planning and Development and the Ministry of Finance and Budget;

The Council adopted a decree ratifying Loan Agreement no. CIV-1032, concluded on 26 February 2025 between the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) and the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire, for a total amount of three million seven hundred and seventy thousand (3,770,000) Islamic Dinars, i.e. three billion seventeen million four hundred and two thousand two hundred (3,017,402,200) CFA Francs, for the financing of the cassava value chain development project in Côte d'Ivoire.

The project covered by these two (02) loan agreements has the overall objective of improving the resilience of the food production system and contributing to the strengthening of food and nutritional security.

More specifically, the project aims to make the cassava value chain more dynamic, from production to processing and marketing of cassava products, with a view to creating more employment opportunities, in particular for young people and women, and increasing the incomes of households working in the cassava sector.

B/- INDIVIDUAL MEASURE

Under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and Ivorians Abroad;

The Council gave its agreement for the appointment of Mr MIRMOHAMMAD MEIGONI Seyed Gholamreza as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Islamic Republic of Iran to the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire, with residence in Abidjan.

C/- COMMUNICATIONS

- Under the Minister of Economy, Planning and Development, in conjunction with the Ministry of Finance and Budget and the Ministry of Culture and Francophonie;

The Council adopted a communication on Côte d'Ivoire's participation in the Spring Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group, held from 21 to 26 April 2025 in Washington DC, in the United States.

An important delegation led by the Minister of Economy, Planning and Development took part in these meetings, which were marked by uncertainties in the global economy linked to the current context of escalating customs duties with a worsening of trade tensions. As a result, the prospects for global economic growth, projected at 2.8% in 2025 and 3% in 2026, are down compared with previous projections.

Consequently, the proceedings recommended caution in the conduct of economic policies and the strengthening of international cooperation, with a view to reducing trade tensions.

With regard to Côte d'Ivoire, our country's economic performance was the subject of particular attention from the IMF, the World Bank Group and all bilateral and private sector actors. The IMF, in particular, welcomed the performance recorded in the ongoing implementation of the Economic and Financial Programme signed together, as well as the success of the eurobond issue in CFA francs.

The progress made in the fight against money laundering and the financing of terrorism, as well as the success recorded in debt management operations, were greatly appreciated by all the technical and financial partners met, who reaffirmed their commitment to continue and intensify their cooperation with our country.

- Under the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, in conjunction with the Ministry of Finance and Budget and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and Ivorians Abroad;

The Council adopted a communication on the candidacy of an Ivorian Human Rights Expert in the elections to renew the members of the United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination, scheduled for 26 June 2025 in New York, in the United States.

The mandate of our compatriot Bakary Sidiki DIABY, elected on 24 June 2021 at the 29th session of the States parties to the United Nations International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination, which established the Committee of Experts, expires in June 2025.

Accordingly, the Council instructed the Keeper of the Seals, Minister of Justice and Human Rights, and all the Ministers concerned, to take the appropriate steps to support the candidacy for the renewal of our compatriot's mandate within this major international body for safeguarding Human Rights.

- Under the Ministry of Digital Transition and Digitalisation, in conjunction with the Ministry of the Interior and Security, the Ministry of Finance and Budget, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Integration and Ivorians Abroad, the Ministry for the Promotion of Youth, Professional Integration and Civic Service and the Ministry of Culture and Francophonie;

Ivoire Tech Forum is a platform of international scope initiated by the Government, within the framework of the Digital Transformation Strategy, to connect Ivorian and African digital start-ups to the rest of the world, by showcasing talent, innovations and investment opportunities.

Nearly five hundred (500) participants are thus expected at this Forum, including digital start-ups, large companies, governmental institutions and international investors.

Ivoire Tech Forum 2025 will take place around the theme "Digital technology at the service of all: how new technologies are transforming our daily lives".

In addition, in order to best respond to the current strategic challenges of digital development, there will be exhibitions, panels, practical workshops, start-up competitions and sectoral forums, on cybersecurity and data protection, Artificial Intelligence, technological entrepreneurship and technological Infrastructure.

- Under the Ministry of Employment and Social Protection

The Council heard the report on the celebration of the 2025 edition of Labour Day.

On the occasion of this celebration, the Prime Minister expressed his deep gratitude to the valiant Ivorian population as well as to all workers, whose self-sacrifice and labour sustain the growth and resilience of the national economy.

He wished to recall the significant gains granted to workers in the public and private sectors since 2013, the cumulative financial effort of which amounts to more than 3,700 billion CFA francs.

With regard to the new demands formulated by the Trade Union Centres, the Prime Minister asked the trade unionists to be patient and to trust the Government so that all demands are dealt with within the framework of procedures centred on social dialogue, so as to preserve the major balances of the development momentum begun by our country.

Moreover, during the celebration of this edition of Labour Day, the Prime Minister announced an exceptional derogatory measure decided by the President of the Republic, allowing the opening of access rights to the CMU (Universal Health Coverage) for insured persons in the informal sector, from 02 May until 31 August 2025, i.e. for a period of four (04) months.

Approximately thirteen (13) million first-time insured persons will benefit, without having contributed beforehand, from the services offered by the CMU, in particular access to care and medicines by paying only the 30% co-payment.

In rural health centres, coverage under this measure is completely free; consultations, nursing procedures and the dispensing of outpatient medicines are covered 100% by the State.

The cost of implementing this decision is estimated at 8.4 billion CFA francs.

D- MISCELLANEOUS

- The Council heard the report of the Vice-President of the Republic, representative of the President of the Republic at the inauguration ceremony of the elected President of the Gabonese Republic, His Excellency Mr Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguéma.

On the sidelines of the ceremony, the President of the Gabonese Republic granted an audience to the Vice-President of the Republic, which focused essentially on strengthening cooperation between the two countries.

- The next Council of Ministers will be held on 22 May 2025 in Abidjan.

Done at Abidjan, Wednesday 07 May 2025

Mr Amadou COULIBALY
Minister of Communication, Government Spokesperson

MASERU – The Directorate on Corruption and Economic Offences (DCEO) has quashed claims that it has halted investigations into the M200 million for the construction Lesotho Standards Institute funded by the African Development Bank (AfDB).
Last month the Ministry of Trade informed Public Eye that the deal for LSI, which is located at Ha Tikoe on the outskirts of the capital Maseru, was above board and DCEO had cleared them to go ahead with the facility.
However, this week the anti-corruption body via its spokesperson, ‘Matlhokomelo Senoko was emphatic that investigations were proceeding.
“I asked the investigator conducting the matter and I was informed that as far he knows he’s continuing with the probe.
“The investigator was told by the Ministry’s Procurement Director, Seriti Khabisi about the alleged letter clearing the department,” Senoko said.
She maintained that the novel anti-graft head, Director General Advocate Brigadier Mantšo Sello is yet to appraise himself with the contents of the said case.
“We are currently under a new management, this case (LSI [mis] procurement) is identified for investigations,” she said.
After raising the flag, Khabisi was suspended for insisting that her office was not consulted according to those privy to the matter.
Khabisi confirmed to this paper that indeed she was on suspension but has since launched a case before courts.
The ministry’s Principal Secretary (PS) Palesa Matobako when contacted said then that the deal was above-board.
“The tender was even investigated by DCEO (Directorate on Corruption and Economic Offences) which indicated that there was no foul-play in the awarding of the tender,” Matobako said.
Matobako confirmed that Khabisi asked the anti-corruption agency to investigate the tender which “was cleared as legal procedures were followed…she (Khabisi) has an axe to grind.”
“She has been suspended for buying phones and placing adverts in newspapers without following proper procedures not what is being peddled,” the PS said.
Last week this paper revealed that AfDB was pissed off by lack of information and the breaking of its rules by government in commencing with the construction at the project site while pre-requisites such as an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) had not been done – as well as the acquisition of a building permit.
“The AfDB made it clear that there is no way that they can support either the construction or purchase of equipment to be installed whilst commencement of the project is surrounded by so many dubious issues and with relevant ministries failing to provide required answers,” a source told this paper.
Last month Minister of Public Works and Transport, Neo Matjato Moteane, sensationally revealed that Trade has not given them official documents relating to the construction of LSI.
A low-spirited Moteane informed Public Eye that as principal agents, standard practice documents related to the edifice have not reached his office; thus, exposing poor coordination between the two ministries.
“We have not seen documents of the building although we are empowered to as a way of supervising such projects; trade has not yet opened doors for us.
“We need a letter that indicates that X Company has been awarded a contract, but we have not received such documentation,” Moteane indicated.
He further highlighted that since the LSI building has been on and off, it makes it difficult for him to track its progress.
For his part, Minister of Trade Mokhethi Shelile explicitly said, “An EIA is not a requirement,” before dropping the phone and informing these reporters to speak to Principal Secretary Palesa Matobako.
However, Matobaka has since indicated that she will never give an interview to this paper.
The construction, as per investigations, goes against the Building Control Act, 1995, since Moteane indicated that he hasn’t received any form of documentation.
Under Part III Duties and Powers of Building Authorities Approval by building authorities of the application in respect of the building operations section 18 (1) read with (2) reads: “(1) No person shall, without the prior approval in writing of the building authority in question, commence any building; (2) A person who contravenes or fails to comply with subsection (1) commits an offense and is liable on conviction to the penalties prescribed in the regulations.”
Adding more pressure, according to the Act, 18 subsection (5) stipulates that “the Ministry of Works shall, in respect of all government buildings, submit all plans, speciﬁcations, documents, or information as may be required under this Act to the building authority in whose jurisdiction building operations will be carried out.”
The E-Regulations website lists twenty-four steps required before starting any construction work for big projects, of which the Land Administration Authority (LAA), Maseru City Council (MCC), Water Sewage Company (WASCO), Lesotho Electricity (LEC), Maseru Fire Brigade, and Roads Directorate are stakeholders.
LSI construction was also identified by Minister of Finance, Dr Retšelisitsoe Matlanyane, during her 2025/2026 budget speech, noting that it is meant “to improve market access, the Lesotho Standards Institution (LSI) will be operationalized to handle standards development, testing, and certification. Construction of LSI facilities will begin in the upcoming financial year.”
The current chief accounting officer, Matobako simply ignored the red flags notwithstanding issues raised.
This is against articles in this publication indicating that government is aware of the Lesotho Promotion and Marketing Services (LPMS) building located in the Maseru Industrial Area, where LSI equipment is stored.
The Ministry of Trade was denied access to their equipment by the infamous Yan “John” Xie on account that the government owes him, according to the PS.
According to her, before Parliament’s Economic Cluster, they (ministry) then went for inspection with Revenue Services Lesotho (RSL) and the marketing department staff where they subsequently met John who indicated he has a signed sub-lease for the building in question.
She indicated that there’s a joint venture agreement with Africomforter where the ministry bought machines for manufacturing duvet covers which are placed in LPMS building.
“John said he was not going to grant us permission to the building because the government owes him, although he did not disclose the amount”, she said, further narrating, “After that incident, we concluded with RSL to open a case in court because what we need is our property and a month after, we requested to have access to at least one machine to continue work and we were granted only that one machine.”
She highlighted that to date, they still have not been assisted.

Niamey, 25 juillet (ANP) -Le fonds de solidarité pour la sauvegarde de la patrie (FSSP), organe de financement endogène mis en place par le Conseil national pour la sauvegarde de la patrie (CNSP) a mobilisé plus de 13 milliards de francs CFA en moins d’un an, auprès des bonnes volontés et des contribuables nigériens.
Ces ressources sont constituées des contributions volontaires des citoyens, des institutions et organisations œuvrant dans le pays, mais aussi des prélèvements financiers effectués auprès des fournitures de certains services publics.
Le Conseil National pour la Sauvegarde de la patrie (CNSP), qui dirige le Niger depuis le 26 juillet 2023, priorise les sources de financements internes pour faire face aux sanctions imposées au pays par ses partenaires financiers et régionaux. C’est la raison de la création du fonds de solidarité pour la sauvegarde de la patrie (FSSP).
Institué par ordonnance du 11 octobre 2023, le FSSP a pour but d’accompagner le CNSP à assurer une transition réussie, dans un contexte difficile caractérisé par des sanctions qui pèsent lourdes sur le pays. L’objectif premier du fonds est la mobilisation de ressources à l’échelle nationale et internationale en vue de subvenir aux dépenses liées à la préservation de la souveraineté nationale.
Cet organe de financement souverain a officiellement lancé ses activités le 31 octobre 2023. Sa plateforme digitale permettant aux citoyens résidents dans le pays, la diaspora et les partenaires du pays de s’informer et aussi de pouvoir contribuer au financement du pays.
Le fonds, par l’appel à la contribution volontaire pour la sécurité et la reconstruction du Niger, a suscité une réponse enthousiaste et un soutien massif de la part des citoyens, tant à l’intérieur du pays qu’à l’étranger.
La plateforme digitale, en plus de la mission d’information, permet également le suivi de la traçabilité des fonds collectés et leur utilisation, pour une transparence « totale et responsable ».
Pour une transparence dans la réception des contributions et pour informer le public, le comité du fonds communique à travers ses pages et dans les médias, avec la sortie de son bulletin hebdomadaire sur la récapitulation des contributions volontaires reçues de la part de la population, des entreprises publiques ou privées, et tout autre opérateur économique, ainsi que des ONG, associations, projets et programmes de développement, mais également sur des prélèvements, avec un total de plus de 13 milliards CFA.
Le fonds sert à la mobilisation des ressources et au financement des appuis au renforcement des capacités des Forces de Défenses et de Sécurité engagées dans la lutte contre le terrorisme et l’insécurité en les dotant d’armement et de moyens logistiques notamment du matériel de transport ; la participation à la prise en charge des citoyens victimes de déplacement forcé lié à l’insécurité, leur relocalisation, leur réintégration locale et retour volontaire ; la prise en Charge de la mobilisation sociale des populations dans le cadre des actions citoyennes.
Les ressources du FSSP seront, en outre, constituées sous forme de Fonds d’investissement en faveur de l’Emploi des Jeunes et des femmes.
Les ressources du fonds sont : le prélèvement sur certaines rubriques de la structure des prix des hydrocarbures ;un prélèvement de10% sur les recettes provenant des redevances annuelles versées à l’Agence de Régulation des Communications Electroniques et de la Poste (ARCEP) par les opérateurs titulaires d’une licence, d’une convention ou d’une autorisation ;un prélèvement de 10% sur les recettes provenant des redevances annuelles pour l’exploitation des services de radiodiffusion et de télévision nationale et internationale, versées à l’autorité en charge de la régulation de la Communication.
Il est également prévu un prélèvement de 10% sur le montant de toute exonération d’impôts accordée par l’Etat à toute structure, entreprise ou société, publique ou privée, bénéficiant des régimes dérogatoires ; un prélèvement de 100 francs CFA par contrat d’assurance émis et encaissé par les compagnies d’assurance ; un prélèvement de 10 francs CFA par mois et par abonné d’une formule au Bouquet-télé souscrit ; un prélèvement de 10% sur les recettes provenant de la redevance de régulation, versées à l’Autorité de Régulation de la Commande Publique (ARCOP) ; un prélèvement de 10 francs CFA sur les tickets de transport terrestre et de péage routier ainsi qu’un prélèvement de mille (1000) francs CFA sur les tickets de transport aérien ; un prélèvement de 10 francs CFA sur chaque appel et chaque souscription au forfait internet et voix; un prélèvement de 10% sur la taxe sur les nuitées d’hôtels.
Le FSSP reçoit aussi les contributions volontaires financières ou en nature des populations, des entreprises publiques, des entreprises privées et de tout autre opérateur économique ainsi que des ONG, associations, projets et programmes de développement ; des contributions volontaires financières et en nature de la Diaspora.
Ainsi, les prélèvements et les contributions en numéraire sont versés dans le compte spécial ouvert dans les écritures du Trésorier Général du Niger ou dans un compte ouvert dans une banque de la place.
Les contributions en nature sont déposées auprès du secrétariat permanent du Conseil National pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie au niveau national et auprès des autorités administratives au niveau territorial.
Les contributions collectées à l’extérieur du Niger sont déposées auprès des services des ambassades et des consulats du Niger ou auprès des représentants du Haut Conseil des Nigériens à l’extérieur.
« Pour le Conseil National pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie (CNSP), les ressources mobilisées doivent constituer une école et un outil dans l’exercice de la bonne gouvernance, un modèle de participation populaire à la conquête de la souveraineté alimentaire et économique. En somme, faire du FSSP un instrument financier pour les nigériens et par les nigériens », a déclaré la présidente du FSSP.
Ainsi le FSSP aspire à consolider l’élan patriotique des citoyens nigériens, à rallier la diaspora, et à solliciter la solidarité du peuple en faveur des droits de l’homme. Cette initiative revêt une importance capitale pour faire face aux défis qui se dressent devant la nation et pour préserver l’intégrité de la patrie nigérienne.
C’est dans ce souci patriotique que la présidente du fond Mme Brah Reki Djermakoye a initié des Séries de rencontres, ainsi les membres du Comité de Gestion du Fonds de Solidarité pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie FSSP et quelques acteurs clés devant concourir à l’alimentation de ce fonds, s’agit d’une rencontre avec les responsables des compagnies de téléphonie mobile et des responsables des compagnies de transports terrestres,
Le comité de gestion du FSSP a rencontré les artistes et les acteurs culturels, cette rencontre entre dans le cadre des consultations entamées par le FSSP pour l’adoption de sa stratégie de communication.
Ils ont également rencontré les centrales syndicales, les agences de voyage et de tourisme, les organisations patronales des gares, les secteurs bancaires du Niger, les associations religieuses, les jeunes leader, les organisations féminines, l’association des chef traditionnels, les ONG internationales, les responsables dés hôtel, le syndicat des huissiers, les FDS , les représentants de l’ecogar, les ordres professionnels … etc. toutes ces rencontres on y pour but de présenter le FSSP et ensuite échanger avec eux sur comment chacun peut amené sa contribution.
Le comité de gestion a également effectué une tournée dans toutes les 5 communes de la capitale Niamey, et a également été dans les régions pour des séances de sensibilisation et d’échange sur la mobilisation, leur présenter le fonds et pour la collecte des contributions.
Lancée officiellement le 31 octobre 2023, la plateforme digitale permettra à tous les Nigériens, d’ici comme de la diaspora, de s’informer et aussi de pouvoir contribuer au Fonds de Solidarité pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie. Cela est possible sur smartphone, tablette ou ordinateur. Les nigériens, comme les amis du Niger pourront désormais participer à leur convenance à cet élan de solidarité pour la dignité de notre pays.
La plateforme digitale, en plus de la mission d’information, permettra le suivi de la traçabilité des fonds collectés et leur utilisation, pour une transparence totale et responsable.
Cet ainsi que plusieurs bonnes volontés au plan national et international expriment leur solidarité.
Le comité de gestion du Fonds de Solidarité pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie (FSSP), poursuit la mobilisation des contributions, la présidente du FSSP Mme Brah Reki Hassane Djermakoye procède à la réception de plusieurs contributions en numéraire et en nature provenant des filles et fils de la nation partout où ils se trouvent dans les quartiers, les cantons, les hameaux, de la diaspora.
Pour une transparence dans la réception des contributions et pour informer le public, le comité du fonds communique à travers ses pages et dans les médias, avec la sortie de leurs bulletin hebdomadaire sur la récapitulation des contributions volontaires reçues de la part de la population, des entreprises publiques ou privées, et tout autre opérateurs économiques, ainsi que des ONG, associations, projets et programme de développement mais également sur des prélèvements, avec un total de plus de 13 milliards cfa au compteur actuellement.
Mme Brah Reki Hassane Djermakoye, une icône du secteur des finances au Niger est à la tête de l’Institution.

Solidarity fund in Niger: More than 13 billion CFA francs mobilised in a patriotic surge - Nigerien Press Agency

Niamey, 25 July (ANP) - The Solidarity Fund for the Safeguarding of the Homeland (FSSP), an endogenous financing body set up by the National Council for the Safeguarding of the Homeland (CNSP), has mobilised more than 13 billion CFA francs in less than a year from people of goodwill and Nigerien taxpayers.

These resources consist of voluntary contributions from citizens, institutions and organisations operating in the country, but also of financial levies collected on the supply of certain public services.

The National Council for the Safeguarding of the Homeland (CNSP), which has led Niger since 26 July 2023, prioritises internal sources of financing in order to face the sanctions imposed on the country by its financial and regional partners. That is the reason for the creation of the Solidarity Fund for the Safeguarding of the Homeland (FSSP).

Established by an ordinance of 11 October 2023, the FSSP aims to support the CNSP in ensuring a successful transition, in a difficult context marked by sanctions that weigh heavily on the country. The fund's primary objective is the mobilisation of resources at national and international level in order to meet expenditure linked to the preservation of national sovereignty.

This sovereign financing body officially launched its activities on 31 October 2023. Its digital platform allows citizens resident in the country, the diaspora and the country's partners to obtain information and also to contribute to the country's financing.

Through the call for voluntary contributions for the security and reconstruction of Niger, the fund has aroused an enthusiastic response and massive support from citizens, both inside the country and abroad.

The digital platform, in addition to its information mission, also allows the traceability of the funds collected and their use to be monitored, for "total and responsible" transparency.

For transparency in the receipt of contributions and to inform the public, the fund's committee communicates through its pages and in the media, with the release of its weekly bulletin recapitulating the voluntary contributions received from the population, from public or private companies and any other economic operator, as well as from NGOs, associations, development projects and programmes, and also on the levies, with a total of more than 13 billion CFA.

The fund serves to mobilise resources and to finance support for strengthening the capacities of the Defence and Security Forces engaged in the fight against terrorism and insecurity, by providing them with weaponry and logistical means, notably transport equipment; participation in caring for citizens who are victims of forced displacement linked to insecurity, their relocation, their local reintegration and voluntary return; and covering the social mobilisation of populations within the framework of citizen actions.

The FSSP's resources will, in addition, be constituted in the form of an Investment Fund in favour of the Employment of Young People and Women.

The fund's resources are: a levy on certain items of the price structure of hydrocarbons; a 10% levy on revenue from the annual royalties paid to the Regulatory Authority for Electronic Communications and Post (ARCEP) by operators holding a licence, a convention or an authorisation; a 10% levy on revenue from the annual royalties for the operation of national and international radio and television broadcasting services, paid to the authority in charge of regulating Communication.

Also provided for is a 10% levy on the amount of any tax exemption granted by the State to any structure, enterprise or company, public or private, benefiting from derogatory regimes; a levy of 100 CFA francs per insurance contract issued and cashed by insurance companies; a levy of 10 CFA francs per month and per subscriber to a television-package formula subscribed; a 10% levy on revenue from the regulation royalty paid to the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (ARCOP); a levy of 10 CFA francs on land transport and road toll tickets as well as a levy of one thousand (1000) CFA francs on air transport tickets; a levy of 10 CFA francs on each call and each subscription to an internet and voice package; and a 10% levy on the tax on hotel overnight stays.

The FSSP also receives voluntary financial or in-kind contributions from the population, public enterprises, private enterprises and any other economic operator as well as from NGOs, associations, development projects and programmes; and voluntary financial and in-kind contributions from the Diaspora.

Thus, the levies and contributions in cash are paid into the special account opened in the books of the Treasurer General of Niger or into an account opened in a local bank.

In-kind contributions are deposited with the permanent secretariat of the National Council for the Safeguarding of the Homeland at national level and with the administrative authorities at territorial level.

Contributions collected outside Niger are deposited with the services of Niger's embassies and consulates or with the representatives of the High Council of Nigeriens Abroad.

"For the National Council for the Safeguarding of the Homeland (CNSP), the resources mobilised must constitute a school and a tool in the exercise of good governance, a model of popular participation in the conquest of food and economic sovereignty. In short, to make the FSSP a financial instrument for Nigeriens and by Nigeriens," declared the president of the FSSP.

Thus the FSSP aspires to consolidate the patriotic surge of Nigerien citizens, to rally the diaspora, and to call on the solidarity of the people in favour of human rights. This initiative is of capital importance in facing the challenges confronting the nation and in preserving the integrity of the Nigerien homeland.

It is in this patriotic concern that the fund's president, Mrs Brah Reki Djermakoye, has initiated a series of meetings; thus the members of the Management Committee of the Solidarity Fund for the Safeguarding of the Homeland (FSSP) and some key actors expected to contribute to feeding this fund held a meeting with the heads of mobile telephone companies and the heads of land transport companies.

The FSSP management committee met artists and cultural actors; this meeting falls within the framework of the consultations begun by the FSSP for the adoption of its communication strategy.

They also met the trade union federations, travel and tourism agencies, employers' organisations of the bus stations, Niger's banking sectors, religious associations, young leaders, women's organisations, the association of traditional chiefs, international NGOs, hotel managers, the bailiffs' union, the Defence and Security Forces, the representatives of the ecogar, the professional orders, etc. All these meetings aim to present the FSSP and then to discuss with them how each can bring their contribution.

The management committee also carried out a tour of all 5 communes of the capital Niamey, and also went to the regions for awareness-raising and discussion sessions on mobilisation, to present the fund to them and to collect contributions.

Officially launched on 31 October 2023, the digital platform will allow all Nigeriens, both here and from the diaspora, to obtain information and also to contribute to the Solidarity Fund for the Safeguarding of the Homeland. This is possible on a smartphone, tablet or computer. Nigeriens, like friends of Niger, will henceforth be able to take part at their convenience in this surge of solidarity for the dignity of our country.

The digital platform, in addition to its information mission, will allow the traceability of the funds collected and their use to be monitored, for total and responsible transparency.

It is thus that many people of goodwill at national and international level express their solidarity.

The management committee of the Solidarity Fund for the Safeguarding of the Homeland (FSSP) continues the mobilisation of contributions; the president of the FSSP, Mrs Brah Reki Hassane Djermakoye, receives numerous contributions in cash and in kind coming from the daughters and sons of the nation wherever they are, in the neighbourhoods, the cantons, the hamlets, and the diaspora.

For transparency in the receipt of contributions and to inform the public, the fund's committee communicates through its pages and in the media, with the release of their weekly bulletin recapitulating the voluntary contributions received from the population, from public or private companies and any other economic operators, as well as from NGOs, associations, development projects and programmes, and also on the levies, with a total of more than 13 billion CFA on the counter at present.

Mrs Brah Reki Hassane Djermakoye, an icon of the finance sector in Niger, is at the head of the Institution.

HER/CA/KPM/ANP 0145 July 2024

Dar es Salaam. Tundu Lissu, mshtakiwa katika kesi ya uhaini amechuana kwa maswali na shahidi wa kwanza wa Jamhuri, mchuano uliodumu kwa takribani saa sita.
Lissu, ambaye ni Mwenyekiti wa Chama cha Demokrasia na Maendeleo (Chadema), anakabiliwa na shtaka la uhaini kinyume na kifungu cha 39(2)(d) cha Sheria ya Kanuni ya Adhabu, linalotokana na maneno anayodaiwa kutamka kuhusu kuzuia kufanyika kwa Uchaguzi Mkuu wa mwaka 2025. Anadaiwa kutenda kosa hilo Aprili 3, 2025, jijini Dar es Salaam.
Maneno yaliyoko kwenye hati ya mashtaka yanayodaiwa kutengeneza kosa la uhaini yanasomeka: "Wakisema msimamo huu unaashiria uasi, ni kweli..., kwa sababu tunasema tutazuia uchaguzi, tutahamasisha uasi, hivyo ndivyo namna ya kupata mabadiliko..., kwa hiyo tunaenda kukinukisha..., sana sana huu uchaguzi tutaenda kuuvuruga kwelikweli..., tunaenda kukinukisha vibaya sana..."
Kesi hiyo, inayosikilizwa na Jaji Mfawidhi wa Mahakama Kuu Masjala Ndogo Iringa, Dunstan Ndunguru (kiongozi wa jopo), na Majaji James Karayemaha na Ferdinand Kiwonde, imeendelea leo, Oktoba 7, 2025, kwa ushahidi wa upande wa Jamhuri.
Lissu amemhoji maswali ya dodoso shahidi wa kwanza wa Jamhuri, Kamishna Msaidizi wa Polisi (ACP) George Bagyemu, ambaye ni Naibu Mkuu wa Upelelezi wa Makosa ya Jinai Kanda Maalumu Dar es Salaam (DZCO).
Mshtakiwa, ambaye anajitetea mwenyewe, amehoji shahidi maswali hayo kuhusu ushahidi alioutoa jana, Oktoba 6, akiongozwa na Wakili wa Serikali Mkuu, Nassoro Katuga.
Sehemu ya mahojiano hayo ni kama ifuatavyo:
Lissu: Waeleze majaji, kama maudhui yenye uchochezi kwa umma ni kosa la uhaini au siyo kosa la uhaini?
Shahidi: Ni kosa la uhaini.
Lissu: Twende kwenye sheria kwanza. Shahidi, jana ulisema kosa la uhaini lipo katika kifungu 39(2)(e) cha Sheria ya Kanuni ya Adhabu?
Shahidi: Ndiyo.
Lissu: Nikupe usome hicho kifungu?
Shahidi: Soma tu wewe.
Lissu: Naomba nikusomee maneno ambayo nimeshtakiwa nayo (anasoma shtaka lake lote). Leo nipo gerezani siku 182, je, maneno haya yapo kwenye hati ya mashtaka?
Shahidi: Hayo uliyoyasoma hayapo, ila yapo kwenye maelezo yangu ya onyo.
Lissu: Kwenye haya niliyosoma, yapo kwenye hati ya mashtaka, kuna sehemu yoyote nimetaja neno la Serikali?
Shahidi: Ndiyo, ukisoma mpaka mwisho utaona.
Lissu: Neno Serikali lipo kwenye hiyo hati ya mashtaka?
Shahidi: Sijui unatafsiri vipi? Lipo.
Lissu: Narudia (anasoma hati ya mashtaka) sasa bwana Kamishna Msaidizi wa Polisi, kama kuna neno Serikali nimelitaja.
Shahidi: Yapo.
Lissu: Waheshimiwa majaji, naomba shahidi ajibu kwa jinsi ninavyomuuliza.
Jaji Ndunguru: Kama shahidi anasema yapo, na wewe unasema hayapo, na hati ya mashtaka mahakama inayo, basi mahakama yenyewe ndiyo ina wajibu wa kujua kama yapo au hayapo.
Lissu: Naomba shahidi ajibu kama kuna maneno Halmashauri ya Jiji la Dar es Salaam, Kinondoni, Ubungo, Temeke, kama yapo kwenye hati ya mashtaka.
Shahidi: Hayapo... hata Manispaa ya Kigamboni hakuna.
Lissu: Waeleze majaji kama kwenye kosa la uhaini kuna maneno ya Rais wa Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania, Samia Suluhu Hassan.
Shahidi: Hayapo.
Lissu: Waambie kama katika maneno ya kihaini kuna maneno Makamu wa Rais wa Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania, Dk Philip Mpango, yapo au hayapo?
Shahidi: Hayapo.
Lissu: Kama katika hayo maelezo yanayodaiwa kuwa ni uhaini kuna cheo chochote cha kiongozi wa ngazi yoyote ya kiserikali?
Shahidi: Hakuna cheo cha kiongozi yoyote kwa ngazi yoyote.
Lissu: Katika hayo maneno kama kuna jina la mamlaka yoyote ya kiserikali ya ngazi yoyote, mfano Mtaa wa Mchafukoge, kama yametajwa kwenye hati ya mashtaka?
Shahidi: Hakuna.
Lissu: Shahidi, waeleze iwapo katika hayo maelezo yanayodaiwa kuwa ni uhaini, kama kuna Mkuu wa Mkoa wa Dar es Salaam, Albert Chalamila.
Shahidi: Hakuna.
Lissu: Serikali ni nini?
Shahidi: Serikali inatokana na neno la Kiajemi, ambalo maana yake ni mamlaka au ni watu na taasisi ndani ya jamii zenye mamlaka ya kiutawala. Pia, kunakuwa na kanuni ambazo zinafuatwa kwa ajili ya kulinda kanuni na taratibu zilizopo.
Lissu: Unafahamu kuhusu serikali ya ndani ya Katiba?
Shahidi: Ndiyo.
Lissu: Naomba usome Ibara ya 151(1) ya Katiba ya Jamhuri ya Muungano.
Shahidi: Serikali maana yake ni Serikali ya Jamhuri ya Muungano, Serikali ya Mapinduzi ya Zanzibar, na mtu yeyote anayetekeleza mamlaka kwa niaba ya Serikali.
Lissu: Naomba uwaeleze majaji, aliyekuelekeza kufungua jalada la uhaini alikuwa ni DCI, Ramadhani Kingai na DCP, Ramadhani Ng’anzi.
Shahidi: Sikuelekezwa, mimi mwenyewe nilifungua baada ya kuona upelelezi unajitosheleza.
Lissu: Katika miaka 22 ya kufanya kazi Jeshi la Polisi, umefanya uchunguzi kwenye kesi kubwa ngapi za kisiasa au zenye umuhimu kwa umma kama hii?
Shahidi: Nimewahi kufanya kesi nne.
Lissu: Zitaje.
Shahidi: Ya Dk Willibrod Slaa.
Lissu: Eeh! Ile ya kuchapisha taarifa za uongo, iliishia wapi?
Shahidi: Sijui ilipoishia. Nyingine ni ya Lembeli kule Kahama.
Lissu: Wakati akiwa mbunge au baada ya ubunge?
Shahidi: Huyo Lembeli alikuwa ni public figure (mtu maarufu)?
Lissu: Sijui unatumia kigezo gani? Ulishafanya uchunguzi kesi ngapi za mtu muhimu na mkubwa kwenye siasa kama Tundu Lissu?
Shahidi: Zipo nne, ikiwamo ya John Heche kule Tarime.
Lissu: Eeh! Hiyo ya Heche ulichunguza halafu ikaishia wapi?
Shahidi: Ilifutwa kwa Nolle (kwamba aliyeifungua haendelei na kesi).
Lissu: Katika kazi yako ndani ya miaka 22 ukiwa ofisa wa Polisi, hakuna kesi yoyote uliyochunguza na ikafikia mwisho na mahakama ikatoa hukumu?
Shahidi: Hakuna.
Lissu: Hakuna kesi yoyote uliyochunguza ikafikia mwisho, yaani ikatolewa hukumu, ukiachana na hii ambayo ipo hapa mahakamani?
Shahidi: Hakuna, ila ya Tundu Lissu itafika mwisho.
Lissu: Kwa ufahamu wako, kwa nini unasema maneno niliyosema siku ile ya kuita waandishi wa habari yalikuwa ni kosa la uhaini?
Shahidi: Ndiyo, yalikuwa ya kosa la uhaini.
Lissu: Hata wewe Polisi, kuita waandishi wa habari wakusikilize ni kosa la uhaini?
Shahidi: Inategemea.
Lissu: Lengo la uhaini lazima lionekane kwa matendo au machapisho au mchoro.
Shahidi: Ni sahihi.
Lissu: Aliyepeleka hayo maneno kwenye mtandao wa Jambo TV ni shahidi P?
Shahidi: Siyo kweli.
Lissu: Aliyerusha maneno hayo kwenye mtandao ni P (shahidi anayelindwa kisheria)?
Shahidi: Ni P na Tundu Lissu.
Lissu: Sasa kwa nini P hajashtakiwa?
Shahidi: Hajashtakiwa kwa sababu ni mwandishi wa habari na hakuja kwako kwenye mkutano wako ili taarifa akaweke jikoni kwake. Huyo P alitueleza baada ya mkutano wa Mwenyekiti wa Chadema, waandishi walitolewa nje ya ukumbi.
Lissu: Huo mkutano na waandishi wa habari ulifanyikia wapi, Mikocheni?
Shahidi: Sijui.
Lissu: Wewe ofisa mzima wa Polisi hujui mkutano ulifanyika wapi, na ndiyo umepeleleza kesi hii?
Shahidi: Hamkutualika.
Lissu: Ulimhoji John Mnyika, Ofisa Habari wa Chadema, Brenda Rupia, juu ya utaratibu wa kualika waandishi wa habari?
Shahidi: Sikumhoji.
Lissu: Waeleze majaji kama mlihoji viongozi wengine wa chama (Chadema) kuhusu utaratibu wa kualika waandishi wa habari.
Shahidi: Hatukuhoji.
Lissu: Ila mimi ndiyo umening’ang’ania?
Shahidi: Ndiyo.
Lissu: Waeleze majaji kama mimi ni mmoja wa wakurugenzi wa Jambo TV.
Shahidi: Sina uhakika wa hilo.
Lissu: Waeleze majaji kama mimi, Tundu Lissu, nina password ya mtandao wa Jambo TV.
Shahidi: Siwezi kufahamu.
Lissu: Kama unajua nina password, waeleze majaji jinsi nilivyoingia kwenye mtandao wa Jambo TV na kuweka hizo picha mjongeo.
Shahidi: Sijui.
Lissu: Waeleze majaji kama wakati unaandika maelezo uliomba ushauri kwa wanasheria.
Shahidi: Sikuomba ushauri.
Lissu: Nani aliyekuambia unaruhusiwa kujiandikia maelezo yako ya onyo mwenyewe?
Shahidi: Hakuna sheria wala kifungu kinachonizuia kuandika maelezo yangu.
Lissu: Nani aliyekukanya?
Shahidi: Sheria ndiyo iliyonikanya.
Lissu: Shahidi, naomba ujibu swali langu, nani aliyekukanya?
Shahidi: Mimi mwenyewe ndiyo niliyejikanya.
Lissu: Nani aliyekuthibitishia hayo maelezo yako uliyoandika?
Shahidi: Mimi mwenyewe, kwa sababu hakuna sheria inayonizuia.
Lissu: Tangu nimetoka JKT, nimeajiriwa na JKT?
Shahidi: Hujaajiriwa, lakini wewe ni askari wa akiba.
Lissu: Hawa askari wa akiba wana masharti sawa na wengine kujiunga na vyama vya siasa?
Shahidi: Sifahamu.
Mahakama imeahirisha kesi hiyo hadi kesho, Oktoba 8, 2025, ambapo Lissu ataendelea kumhoji maswali ya dodoso shahidi huyo.
a639.en:
Dar es Salaam. Tundu Lissu, the accused in the treason case, has traded questions with the first prosecution witness, a contest that lasted for about six hours.

Lissu, who is the Chairman of the Party for Democracy and Progress (Chadema), faces a charge of treason contrary to section 39(2)(d) of the Penal Code Act, arising from words he is alleged to have uttered about preventing the holding of the 2025 General Election. He is alleged to have committed the offence on 3 April 2025, in Dar es Salaam.

The words in the charge sheet which are alleged to constitute the offence of treason read: "When they say this position amounts to rebellion, it is true..., because we say we will block the election, we will incite rebellion, that is the way to obtain change..., so we are going to make it stink..., above all we are really going to disrupt this election..., we are going to make it stink very badly..."

The case, which is being heard by the Judge in Charge of the High Court Sub-Registry of Iringa, Dunstan Ndunguru (head of the panel), and Judges James Karayemaha and Ferdinand Kiwonde, continued today, 7 October 2025, with the prosecution's evidence.

Lissu cross-examined the first prosecution witness, Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) George Bagyemu, who is the Deputy Head of Criminal Investigations for the Dar es Salaam Special Zone (DZCO).

The accused, who is defending himself, questioned the witness on the evidence he gave yesterday, 6 October, when he was led by the Principal State Attorney, Nassoro Katuga.

Part of that examination was as follows:

Lissu: Tell the judges, is content that is seditious to the public a treason offence or not a treason offence?
Witness: It is a treason offence.

Lissu: Let us go to the law first. Witness, yesterday you said the offence of treason is in section 39(2)(e) of the Penal Code Act?
Witness: Yes.

Lissu: Shall I give you that section to read?
Witness: You just read it yourself.

Lissu: Allow me to read out to you the words with which I have been charged (he reads out his whole charge). Today I have been in prison for 182 days; are these words in the charge sheet?
Witness: What you have read is not there, but it is in my cautioned statement.

Lissu: In what I have read, which is in the charge sheet, is there anywhere I mentioned the word Government?
Witness: Yes, if you read to the end you will see it.

Lissu: Is the word Government in that charge sheet?
Witness: I don't know how you are interpreting it? It is there.

Lissu: I repeat (he reads the charge sheet), now Mr Assistant Commissioner of Police, tell me whether there is any word Government that I mentioned.
Witness: They are there.

Lissu: Honourable judges, I ask that the witness answer in the manner in which I am asking him.

Judge Ndunguru: If the witness says they are there, and you say they are not there, and the court has the charge sheet, then the court itself has the duty to determine whether they are there or not.

Lissu: I ask that the witness answer whether there are the words Dar es Salaam City Council, Kinondoni, Ubungo, Temeke, whether they are in the charge sheet.
Witness: They are not there... not even Kigamboni Municipality is there.

Lissu: Tell the judges whether in the treason offence there are the words President of the United Republic of Tanzania, Samia Suluhu Hassan.
Witness: They are not there.

Lissu: Tell them whether in the treasonous words there are the words Vice-President of the United Republic of Tanzania, Dr Philip Mpango; are they there or not?
Witness: They are not there.

Lissu: In those statements alleged to be treason, is there any title of a leader of any level of government?
Witness: There is no title of any leader of any level.

Lissu: In those words, is there the name of any government authority of any level, for example Mchafukoge Street, is it mentioned in the charge sheet?
Witness: There is none.

Lissu: Witness, tell them whether in those statements alleged to be treason there is the Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner, Albert Chalamila.
Witness: There is none.

Lissu: What is a Government?
Witness: "Serikali" comes from a Persian word, which means authority, or it is the people and institutions within society that hold administrative authority. There are also rules that are followed in order to protect the existing rules and procedures.

Lissu: Do you know about government within the Constitution?
Witness: Yes.

Lissu: Please read Article 151(1) of the Constitution of the United Republic.
Witness: Government means the Government of the United Republic, the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar, and any person exercising authority on behalf of the Government.

Lissu: Please tell the judges, the person who directed you to open the treason file was the DCI, Ramadhani Kingai, and the DCP, Ramadhani Ng'anzi.
Witness: I was not directed; I myself opened it after seeing that the investigation was sufficient.

Lissu: In your 22 years working in the Police Force, in how many big political cases or cases of public importance like this one have you conducted investigations?
Witness: I have handled four cases.

Lissu: Name them.
Witness: That of Dr Willibrod Slaa.

Lissu: Ah! That one of publishing false information, where did it end up?
Witness: I don't know where it ended up. Another is that of Lembeli in Kahama.

Lissu: While he was a Member of Parliament or after his time in Parliament?
Witness: Was that Lembeli a public figure (a well-known person)?

Lissu: I don't know what criterion you are using? How many cases have you investigated involving an important and big person in politics like Tundu Lissu?
Witness: There are four, including that of John Heche in Tarime.

Lissu: Ah! That one of Heche that you investigated, where did it end up?
Witness: It was withdrawn by nolle prosequi (meaning the person who filed it did not proceed with the case).

Lissu: In your work over 22 years as a Police officer, is there no case at all that you investigated that reached its conclusion and the court delivered a judgment?
Witness: There is none.

Lissu: There is no case you investigated that reached its conclusion, that is, judgment was delivered, apart from this one that is here in court?
Witness: There is none, but that of Tundu Lissu will reach its conclusion.

Lissu: In your understanding, why do you say the words I spoke that day when I called journalists were a treason offence?
Witness: Yes, they were a treason offence.

Lissu: Even for you, a police officer, is calling journalists to listen to you a treason offence?
Witness: It depends.

Lissu: The intention of treason must be shown by acts or publications or drawings.
Witness: That is correct.

Lissu: The one who put those words on the Jambo TV network is witness P?
Witness: That is not true.

Lissu: The one who broadcast those words on the network is P (a legally protected witness)?
Witness: It is P and Tundu Lissu.

Lissu: So why has P not been charged?
Witness: He has not been charged because he is a journalist and he did not come to you at your meeting in order to put the information in his kitchen. That P told us that after the meeting of the Chadema Chairman, the journalists were taken out of the hall.

Lissu: Where was that meeting with journalists held, Mikocheni?
Witness: I don't know.

Lissu: You, a full police officer, do not know where the meeting was held, and yet you investigated this case?
Witness: You did not invite us.

Lissu: Did you question John Mnyika, or the Chadema Information Officer, Brenda Rupia, about the procedure for inviting journalists?
Witness: I did not question him.

Lissu: Tell the judges whether you questioned other leaders of the party (Chadema) about the procedure for inviting journalists.
Witness: We did not question them.

Lissu: But it is me you have fixed upon?
Witness: Yes.

Lissu: Tell the judges whether I am one of the directors of Jambo TV.
Witness: I am not certain about that.

Lissu: Tell the judges whether I, Tundu Lissu, have the password of the Jambo TV network.
Witness: I cannot know.

Lissu: If you know I have the password, tell the judges how I got into the Jambo TV network and posted those moving pictures.
Witness: I don't know.

Lissu: Tell the judges whether, when you were writing the statement, you sought advice from lawyers.
Witness: I did not seek advice.

Lissu: Who told you that you are allowed to write your own cautioned statement yourself?
Witness: There is no law or section preventing me from writing my statement.

Lissu: Who cautioned you?
Witness: It is the law that cautioned me.

Lissu: Witness, please answer my question, who cautioned you?
Witness: I myself am the one who cautioned myself.

Lissu: Who certified that statement you wrote?
Witness: I myself, because there is no law preventing me.

Lissu: Since I left the JKT (National Service), have I been employed by the JKT?
Witness: You have not been employed, but you are a reserve soldier.

Lissu: Do these reserve soldiers have the same conditions as others regarding joining political parties?
Witness: I do not know.

The court adjourned the case until tomorrow, 8 October 2025, when Lissu will continue to cross-examine that witness.
